fenceDiagnostic.method: Diagnostic gl.flush+fence before first destination copy; wall latency includes command queue, GPU work and main-thread polling delay. Not GPU timer or performance baseline.

passAblation.method: Attribution-only skip entire renderer.render for one pass, retaining previous framebuffer contents. Invalid visuals or frozen buffers, never acceptance/performance gain. Other passes and canvas copies continue. Deltas include upload migration, dependency and cache effects; wall CPU submission is not GPU time.

uploadAblation.method: Attribution-only frozen GPU buffers/textures or all render passes skipped. Invalid/frozen visuals, not a product gain. All uploads/calls restored in finally. Pose generation and destination copies continue; allRender also suppresses upload execution inside Three.

bitmapPresentationProbe.method: Experimental steady-state bitmap injection after ready, same pool/engine/canvases; timing canvases never read. Not production routing or first-ready/lifecycle proof.

noCopyDiagnostic.method: Attribution-only: suppress destination drawImage while clearRect continues; original WebGL draws continue with explicit flush each frame. Blank/invalid displayed avatars, never a product performance result or proposed behavior.

findings: Source Storybook Matrix4 array flatten/toArray sampled self time~1.26seconds/5seconds disappears with immutable flat uniform buffers. Adjacent source steady45.26→49.85fps, but built24 control23.86 vsflat24.53 shows no material production throughput gain in that workload.

24 all-visible authored/categorized actors remain slow on WebView and standalone Chromium; the ceiling is not unique to embedded WebView. Different graphics backends preclude attributing their FPS difference solely to embedding.

During late adjacent controls, skipping depth/color/present separately, all rendering, or GPU buffer/texture uploads fails to materially improve~20–21fps while destination copies continue. Invalid visual diagnostics strongly direct investigation toward browser presentation/interoperation; they do not prove a single internal driver cause.

Atlas ImageBitmap followed by the same24 Canvas2D destinations provides no measurable improvement:104–105 completed batches/5seconds, no stale destinations/fallback/errors. The promise alone does not remove downstream work.
